eps.d: Colonel Ralph Kruger and his army of US combat troops have come across the pond to help out during the Second World War, though when they arrive, Kruger's army immediately enjoys handing out at the bar.
Kruger decides to make the Balaclava Arms pub off limits to enlisted men.
Kruger has started to notice that Pulaski has been off lately, so he assigns Rossi to find out why he's being acting different.
Irving wants Kruger to be more keen on helping out the locals, just like the rest of the platoon. Irving decides to talk to Kruger to get him to change his mind.
Kruger thinks his men have been smuggling limey dames into the camp at night. Pulaski and the others try to hide it from Kruger.
Chambers is throwing a League of Amity club, and he wants Kruger's army to join. Rossi and his mates have a hard time trying to keep there cool, especially Rossi.
Kruger and his army have been told to communicate with Britishers. Kruger doesn't know how to get together with the British, but soon he comes up with an idea.
Aristocrat Lieutenant Beamish Cooke-Cooke is brought in by Irving and his army to instill discipline.
Lady Gertrude offers to help out Irving by tracing his ancestors, but she soon discovers something amiss in his genealogy.
Irving and the platoon grow suspicious of Rossi's secret assignations.
Town clerk Randall Todd organises a Brains Trust at the church hall, and challenges the Americans.

eps.t: Some of Our Coal is Missing
eps.d: When some essential commodities go missing, the culprit, Rossi, is ordered by Irving to appear before the unit psychiatrist.

eps.t: The First of the G.I. Brides
eps.d: Rossi and Doreen are getting married, but when Irving makes a mistake, he must stop the wedding.
